account: Catherine Tan Li Eng, 51, took 19 Jacob's Creek wine bottles worth about S$556 from the Sheng Siong supermarket at Block 622D Punggol Central, Singapore. She bagged them unscanned at self-checkout from 2 to 11 September 2025. On 10 September staff found stock discrepancies, reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV) and uploaded her face to the chain's AI-driven facial recognition system. It automatically identified the earlier thefts. When she returned at noon on 11 September the retail manager got a phone alert. He stopped her at the self-checkout kiosk and found three unscanned bottles. Police arrested her. On 12 May 2026 District Judge Brenda Chua jailed her for eight days on an amalgamated theft charge after full restitution of about S$470.

ai_role.statement: The system's documented contribution came after a human detection. On 10 September 2025 a staff member found discrepancies in a stock check. Colleagues reviewed CCTV and saw Tan leaving without paying. They uploaded her face. The Straits Times reports that the system “then automatically identified the other instances” of theft. That turned one observed theft into an amalgamated charge covering seven visits. On 11 September the system's alert reached the retail manager's phone when she entered. He intercepted her at the self-checkout kiosk with three unscanned bottles. The interception, the bag check, the police call, the prosecution and the restitution were human and institutional. No source names the vendor or the model, gives an accuracy figure, or reports a false match in this case.

fields.account: Catherine Tan Li Eng, 51, took 19 Jacob's Creek wine bottles worth about S$556 from the Sheng Siong supermarket at Block 622D Punggol Central, Singapore. She bagged them unscanned at self-checkout from 2 to 11 September 2025. On 10 September staff found stock discrepancies, reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV) and uploaded her face to the chain's AI-driven facial recognition system. It automatically identified the earlier thefts. When she returned at noon on 11 September the retail manager got a phone alert. He stopped her at the self-checkout kiosk and found three unscanned bottles. Police arrested her. On 12 May 2026 District Judge Brenda Chua jailed her for eight days on an amalgamated theft charge after full restitution of about S$470.

fields.purpose: Sheng Siong rolled out its AI-driven facial recognition CCTV system in April 2024 as a measure against shoplifters. It worked with the Singapore Police Force under its Shop Theft for Retailers (STAR) program. In August 2025 it announced an extension to all 83 outlets. Staff upload the photograph of a suspect identified from footage. The system alerts store managers' phones when that person enters any branch. Sheng Siong said thefts per store rose from 4.91 in 2023 to 8 in 2024. Its CEO attributed the rise to catching cases the human eye had missed. Identifying a repeat shoplifter and flagging her return was exactly its designed purpose.

A repeat offender who came back to the same outlet at noon the next day, which gave the alert something to fire on.

A manager on the premises with his phone, able to intercept at the self-checkout kiosk. A police and court process (the STAR program, an amalgamated theft charge) that turned the identification into restitution and a sentence.

display.answer: A stock check that revealed missing wine led staff to review camera footage and upload the suspect’s face. The system sent an alert that reached the manager when she returned the next day. Staff stopped her at the checkout. Police and court proceedings that followed led to restitution and an eight-day sentence.

fields.account: Catherine Tan Li Eng, 51, took 19 Jacob's Creek wine bottles worth about S$556 from the Sheng Siong supermarket at Block 622D Punggol Central, Singapore. She bagged them unscanned at self-checkout from 2 to 11 September 2025. On 10 September staff found stock discrepancies, reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV) and uploaded her face to the chain's AI-driven facial recognition system. It automatically identified the earlier thefts. When she returned at noon on 11 September the retail manager got a phone alert. He stopped her at the self-checkout kiosk and found three unscanned bottles. Police arrested her. On 12 May 2026 District Judge Brenda Chua jailed her for eight days on an amalgamated theft charge after full restitution of about S$470.

echoes.setting: Malay Mail, 9 October 2026 (AsiaOne report): Leong Seek Yuen, 45, jailed one week after Sheng Siong's facial recognition system alerted staff when she re-entered its Sin Ming Avenue outlet on 1 October 2025, following twelve thefts of meat and drinks worth about S$90 between 27 May and 12 August 2025; as here, an assistant supervisor had first found stock discrepancies and checked CCTV. https://www.malaymail.com/news/singapore/2026/10/09/singapore-supermarkets-facial-recognition-system-catches-woman-after-12-shoplifting-trips/238387

must_hold: The system identifies, it does not detect. Stock counts or staff still have to notice the first theft. Sheng Siong's CEO implied as much when he said the human eye had missed cases.
Someone must act on the alert within minutes. The gain here was an interception before she left the store, not the alert itself.
The match must be right and lawful. A wrong face flagged at the door would produce a wrongful stop. No source reports a false match in this case. None names the vendor or any accuracy figure.
produced_by: A chain-wide facial recognition layer on existing CCTV (rolled out from April 2024, extended to all 83 outlets after August 2025). Staff upload a suspect's face, and managers get app alerts when that person re-enters any branch.
A human trigger: a stock check on 10 September 2025 that revealed missing bottles. Staff then reviewed the footage and uploaded the face the same day.
A repeat offender who came back to the same outlet at noon the next day, which gave the alert something to fire on.

A manager on the premises with his phone, able to intercept at the self-checkout kiosk. A police and court process (the STAR program, an amalgamated theft charge) that turned the identification into restitution and a sentence.

purpose: Sheng Siong rolled out its AI-driven facial recognition CCTV system in April 2024 as a measure against shoplifters. It worked with the Singapore Police Force under its Shop Theft for Retailers (STAR) program. In August 2025 it announced an extension to all 83 outlets. Staff upload the photograph of a suspect identified from footage. The system alerts store managers' phones when that person enters any branch. Sheng Siong said thefts per store rose from 4.91 in 2023 to 8 in 2024. Its CEO attributed the rise to catching cases the human eye had missed. Identifying a repeat shoplifter and flagging her return was exactly its designed purpose.

ratings.reason: Sheng Siong's gain was small and specific. It kept three bottles on 11 September 2025. It got full restitution of about S$470 for the rest of the 19 bottles (about S$556 in all). A seven-visit theft series at one outlet ended. The amount is minor for an 83-outlet chain. The first detection was a human stock check and a manual review of CCTV, not the system.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. the date observed is 11 September 2025, the day the system's alert led to the interception and arrest; the Monitor's 12 May 2026 is the sentencing and reporting date. Filed as benefit created or restored (identification, arrest and restitution for an identifiable organization); the 11 September interception with three unscanned bottles could be read as a small specific harm prevented, but the record's benefit is the identification of the series and the recovery of the loss. Values differ slightly by outlet: CNA about S$556, The Straits Times over $550, AsiaOne over $555; restitution is “about S$470” in CNA and “full restitution” in all three, consistent with the three bottles recovered on 11 September. No source names the vendor of the facial recognition system or a model, so developer and the model version are null; the system's design and the STAR program come from Mothership's 26 August 2025 report of CNA's rollout story, as CNA's own rollout article returned 404 at the URL found and the Yahoo syndication 404 as well. CNA and The Straits Times refused direct fetches and were read through the r.jina.ai text proxy; The Straits Times headline now reads “...caught by Sheng Siong's facial recognition system” while its URL slug and the Monitor's title read “...from Sheng Shiong caught using facial recognition system”. Malay Mail's 12 May 2026 syndication of David Sun's Straits Times piece was read once and returned 403 on re-fetch, so it is not cited; STOMP and The Independent Singapore returned 403. AsiaOne credits The Straits Times and CNA. No source discusses the PDPA or privacy aspects of the system; the record notes that the first detection was human.
